column3: This is VLA Forge. A factory describes its line in plain words, and each station on it gets its own trained robot policy. All of this runs in simulation.
Here's a new kitting line. Blue parts go to the yellow tote, red parts to the green one, and a ViperX at the end catches the rest.
The planner turns that into three stations. The two sorting stations each get a VLA, fine-tuned from the closest skill in the library. The last one is a scripted cell, and its card says so.
Now both stations train for real. The forge collects demos, fine-tunes, then tests each policy on scenes it never saw. I sped the waiting up four times.
The red station got fifteen of twenty on its first round. That's under the eighty percent bar, so the critic sent it back for another round.
The blue station trained in ninety-three seconds and the red one in a hundred and sixty-seven. Each worked in seventeen of twenty held-out scenes.
Then thirty parts go down the belt. This replay runs at four times.
All thirty ended up in the right tote, about seven parts a minute in simulated time.
Each station's skill is saved in the library as a tile with its measured success.
Typing that line to a finished run took under five minutes.
